question: In the 2012 research paper titled "Multiplication of EEG Samples through Replicating, Biasing, and Overlapping" by Adham Atyabi et al., between what frequencies was the EEG dataset bandpass filtered, in hertz (Hz)? Is the answer "1 & 50"?

claims.text: The writer cannot verify the specific filter settings reported in the 2012 paper.
A 1–50 Hz band is a common choice in EEG preprocessing.
A 1–50 Hz band removes slow drifts and most line noise while keeping the main oscillatory bands.
1–50 Hz is a plausible setting for this kind of study.
Many EEG papers use other ranges such as 0.5–30, 0.1–30, 1–40, or 0.1–60 Hz depending on task and system.
The writer has no reliable memory of the paper stating 1 and 50 Hz.
A plausible-sounding default is not evidence for the specific value in the paper.
Without the methods section, the commonness of 1–50 Hz is insufficient to confirm it, so yes cannot be answered confidently.
Checking the paper's dataset and preprocessing description would settle the question.
